Investment

Aschraf Candle

This solemn candle, lit during the Bludish community's Aschraf Anniversary event, softly whispers the stories of unity in diversity. Each flicker echoes with the strength of a people, their history and struggles, painting a picture of resilience and hope.
Car Key

It isn't merely a key, but an emblem of speed, power, and luxury. Its cold metal holds the thrill of driving a sports car, embodying the prestige of the Randolfini brand, a classic Lespian auto giant.
Ceremonial Scissors
A gleaming symbol of progress, these scissors, used to cut ribbons at infrastructure project inaugurations, are a tangible reminder of your contributions to the modern face of Sordland.

Bribery

A gift from Walter Tusk, this box emanates a distinct, rich aroma of tobacco leaves toasted in the Lespian sunshine and rolled by the finest Lespian cigar-makers. Each cigar within it speaks of power, wealth, and the complex intricacies of Sordish and Lespian oligarchy.
King Egmund's Dagger
An ancient relic passed down through generations, this dagger tells tales of King Egmund's reign. A reminder of the weight of leadership, it's more than a weapon—it's a piece of Sordish history.
Sordish Goat Statue
This intricate statue of a Sordish goat stands as a beacon of national pride. Crafted in minute detail, it's a quiet celebration of the country's heritage and natural bounty.
Gun

This stark piece of Sordish weaponry, a stark echo of conflict, weighs heavy with the tension of a nation at war. It serves as a grim reminder of the challenges Sordland faces, and the grit needed to navigate them.
Headphones

These headphones, with their tangle of wires and worn pads, have become your companion in the midst of war. Their soundscape forms a bubble of focus amidst the chaos, providing clarity when it is needed most.
Kesaro's Lighter
A seemingly simple device that once saved a life from a bullet. Every spark it creates illuminates a tale of narrow escapes and unpredictable turns of fate.
Torn Family Photo
This photo, torn at the edges, speaks volumes of love lost and bridges burned. It serves as a poignant reminder of personal sacrifices made in pursuit of national leadership.
Serge's Pocket Watch
A timeless memento of friendship, this watch once belonged to your loyal driver, Serge Wolkner. Each tick whispers stories of camaraderie and loyalty, echoing the rhythm of your shared journey.
Circas's Poem Book
Holding this book is like touching the heart of a fallen poet. Each verse within it echoes with the grief and glory of a nation, and a solitary voice silenced too soon.

Investment
A shining symbol of entrepreneurial success, this trophy marks your investment in Underhall. It stands as an attestation to Sordland's infrastructural growth and the promise of prosperity.
USP Brooch
Worn during the 58 election campaign, this brooch is a symbol of your political journey. Despite its small size, it carries the weight of a nation's hopes and the fierce urgency of change.
Whiskey Bottle
An Erlory maroon, 30 years aged—a bottle of pure harmony, each sip unfolds layers of complex flavors, transporting one to the serene highlands of Sordland.

Section 10: Citizenship & Rights

The term "Sord" will be removed from the Constitution, and Article 7 will be modified to: "Everyone; regardless of language, race, color, gender, political thought, philosophical belief, religion or disability are equal before the law."
Ban on Red Youth
Red Youth is declared as a terrorist organization and a national security threat. The state will take action against its past and current members, and the people who assisted them.
Ban On Workers Party of Bludia

Workers Party of Bludia is declared as the direct successor of the Bludish Freedom Party, and in extension, will be banned from politics for supporting the Bludish Freedom Front. Their members are considered to be national security threats.
Ban On Young Sords
Young Sords is declared as a terrorist organization and a national security threat. The state will take action against its past and current members, and the people who assisted them.
Section 1: Vetoes
No Changes. (Presidents may use their veto on bills without limits.)
Presidential vetoes will be removed from the Constitution.
Article 82 will be modified to include a new process to override a presidential veto with a supermajority in the Grand National Assembly of Sordland.
Article 82 will be modified to include a limit to presidential vetoes but will not define a time limit for a president to act on a bill, giving the presidents an absolute pocket veto power.
Detention Without Trial

Based on strong indications, if the person is suspected of crimes committed against internal and external security, but gathering of incriminating evidence is not possible, the suspect may be proposed to be detained until further notice.
Increased Police Authority
Police’s use of force, orders for confiscations as well as it’s right to stop and frisk, are permissible beyond the legal limits otherwise prescribed.
Section 2: Constitutional Amendments
The Supreme Court's vote will be removed from the constitutional amendments process.
Suspension of Protests and Large Assemblies

The right for peaceful protests is suspended, and in extension the freedom to assemble and organize and the freedom of expression is restricted. The police may use the necessary force to disperse crowds or prevent their gathering.
Severance of Ties With Arcasia

The State severs all of its diplomatic ties with Republic of Arcasia as they pose a national threat to the Republic of Sordland. The State places an embargo on Arcasia, and their citizens will be denied entry to Sordland.
Severance of Ties With Rumburg

The State severs all of its diplomatic ties with the Kingdom of Rumburg as they pose a national threat to the Republic of Sordland. The State places an embargo on Rumburg, and their citizens will be denied entry to Sordland.
Severance of Ties With United Contana

The State severs all of its diplomatic ties with United Contana as they pose a national threat to the Republic of Sordland. The State places an embargo on United Contana, and their citizens will be denied entry to Sordland.
Section 3: Impeachment of the President
No Changes. (Supreme Court may impeach the president on grounds of unconstitutional behavior.)
Article 17 will be modified to include both the Supreme Court and the Grand National Assembly in the impeachment process of the president.
The presidential impeachment process from Article 17 will be removed.
Section 4: Appointment of Ministers
No Changes. (The President appoints the Council of Ministers.)
The President will nominate ministers which will require a confidence vote from the Grand National Assembly for their appointment.
The Grand National Assembly will nominate a list of ministers, which the President may appoint.
Loophole
Section 5: Election Threshold
No Changes. (A political party requires at least 10% of the general vote to win seats in the Grand National Assembly.)
The election threshold will be increased to 15%.
The election threshold will be decreased to 8%
The election threshold will be decreased to 3%.
Section 6: Presidential Decrees
No Changes. (The President may issue decrees in certain subjects without going through the Grand National Assembly.)
Presidential decrees will be removed from the Constitution.
Presidential decrees will require an enabling act to be passed by the Grand National Assembly.
Presidential decrees will be able to be issued in political, social, and economic issues that would carry the force of law, and will not be subject to judicial review.
Section 7: Term Limits
No Changes. (The Constitution doesn't define any term limit.)
A president will not be able to serve more than 2 terms.
Section 8: Impeachment of the Justices
No Changes. (The Constitution gives the Justices of the Supreme Court absolute immunity before the law and describes no procedure of impeachment.)
The Grand National Assembly will have the right to propose an impeachment of a Justice on the legal grounds of unconstitutional behavior.
The President will have the right to appoint and replace the Justices of the Supreme Court.
Section 9: Member of Honor
No Changes. (The Member of Honor has absolute immunity and is considered to be a permanent member of the Grand National Assembly.)
The absolute immunity of the Member of Honor will be removed from Article 99.
Article 99 and the Member of Honor title will be removed from the Constitution.
Every president will be considered a Member of Honor after the end of their service.
